sentences.text:
Author: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Bench: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
 Office Notes,
 reports, orders
Sl. or proceedings
 Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order

S No or directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  ABA 695/2023  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. Ranjan Ghildiyal, AGA, for the State.
Mr. P.C. Petshali, Advocate, for the complainant.

(2) Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with FIR No. 322 of 2023, under Sections 420,
504, 506 IPC, registered with PS Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar.

(3) Learned Counsel for the applicant contended that the allegation against the applicant is that he entered into an agreement to sell with the complainant in respect of a property, which was already pledged with a bank for securing a loan.

It is also contended that maximum jail sentence for the alleged offences is up to seven years, therefore, applicant is entitled to benefit of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in (2014) 8 SCC (4)

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in (2014) 8 SCC (4)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned State Counsel fairly submits that since the offences are punishable with maximum jail sentence of up to seven years, therefore, Investigating Officer shall give notice to the applicant in terms of Section 41-A of CrPC and subject to his complying with the conditions of said notice,
applicant shall not be arrested.
( 5 ) In view of the statement made by learned State Counsel, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of.
However, it is made clear that in case the applicant violates any condition of notice under Section 41-A of CrPC, I.O. shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicant as per law.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 18.8.2023 Pr ABA/695/2023 on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160072814/
